decisions.statement: A flag holding prose is answered by a second flag naming the file that prose sits in.
A value said at its flag and at its file at once is the caller's mistake.
A file named `-` is the input.
A path that is not absolute is read against the root handed over.
A value read whole keeps the line endings at its end, and any other value loses them.
Whether a value is read whole belongs to the filing rather than to the reader.
A file that would not open is answered as a refusal rather than thrown.
A pair of values handed in is read as the same pair looked up in what a call said.

definition: what a command was told at a flag or in the file a flag names
